options: A plain text file of PowerShell commands, run in order — the same commands you could type at the console
A compiled binary that only runs on servers with a special license
A configuration file that PowerShell reads but never executes
A file format unique to Windows PowerShell ISE that VS Code cannot open
questions.explain: There's no special magic to a script — it's saved commands, run in sequence.

questions.q: What does the execution policy actually do?
options: It's a safety setting that blocks scripts from running by default, so a malicious .ps1 file can't silently execute
It controls how fast PowerShell scripts execute on the CPU
It determines which version of PowerShell is installed
It only affects scripts that connect to the internet
questions.explain: Execution policy exists to prevent scripts from running unintentionally, not to manage performance or versions.

questions.q: What does Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser actually change?
options: It lets locally written scripts run freely while requiring downloaded scripts to carry a trusted digital signature, for the current user account only
It disables execution policy entirely for every user on the machine
It only allows scripts written by Microsoft to run
It permanently deletes the current execution policy setting
questions.explain: RemoteSigned is the practical middle ground: your own local scripts run, but internet-downloaded ones need a signature. -Scope CurrentUser limits the change to your account.

questions.q: Why does typing just script.ps1 (without .\) fail even when the file is in your current folder?
options: PowerShell doesn't search the current directory for executables by default — that's a deliberate security choice
PowerShell cannot run any file that ends in .ps1
The file must always be renamed before it can run
Only administrator accounts are allowed to omit the .\ prefix
questions.explain: Unlike cmd.exe, PowerShell won't run a same-named file from the current folder by accident — you have to explicitly reference it with .\ or a full path.

questions.q: What tool from Lesson 2 is the real one for writing .ps1 scripts?
options: VS Code
Microsoft Word
SQL Server Management Studio
Notepad is the only supported option and no other editor works
questions.explain: VS Code, covered in Lesson 2 alongside the console and ISE, is the practical editor for writing real scripts.
